result.title: Exact-Solution Volume and Length Generalization in Transformers
result.summary: Research on transformer expressivity shows whether a transformer is capable of solving a given task, but gives little indication of whether the solution, if learned, is generalizable to longer input lengths. We study this question through normalized exact-solution volume (NESV): the fraction of a bounded parameter region that achieves an exact solution on every input of length $n$. For fixed-width, single-layer transformers with $\log n$-scaled attention, we establish asymptotic bounds on NESV for four tasks: FIRST ($Θ(1)$), MAJORITY ($Θ(1/(n\log n))$), INDEX ($Θ(1/n^3)$), and PARITY ($0$). These results are consistent with previous empirical results: the faster the exact-solution volume decays with input length, the harder it is to length-generalize on that task. Looking deeper into INDEX, our volume analysis reveals two error sources that grow with $n$. Consequently, we study a transformer model that would structurally eliminate one of the terms, theoretically improving the NESV bound to $Θ(n^{-1})$, and empirically achieving 85% accuracy when tested at $10\times$ the training length, compared with the 60% accuracy of the original model. We conclude that volume analysis may be a useful approach to identify concrete sources of length sensitivity and thus provide insights into task-specific model refinements.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出归一化精确解体积（NESV）指标，衡量有界参数区域内能在所有长度 n 输入上精确解任务的比例，对定宽单层、log n 缩放注意力 Transformer 在 FIRST、MAJORITY、INDEX、PARITY 四个任务上给出渐近界，并据 INDEX 的误差来源改造结构使长度泛化精度提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽然对象是纯文本算法任务，但其用参数体积/精确解比例预测长度泛化的思路，可能与 LVR 中推理链长度泛化、workspace 容量与监督信号分配有关，可供核查如何用「解的体积」解释 laten 状态随长度衰减。
